opening_message:
Ticket 1: Michael Cervantes (employee ID E025) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E025.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Michael Cervantes (E025) is a full-time Analyst requesting admin to Source Code. Full-time policy caps at write unless the employee's role owns the system; Analyst does not own Source Code (owned by Engineer), so admin is not permitted. Grant write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security record for E025 shows contractor with basic security training. Contractors max at read without advanced training (admin never allowed). Requested admin to Source Code, so grant read.
reason: Employee E025 (Michael Cervantes) requested admin to Source Code. The Security agent's record, which was looked up in the security database, shows the employee is a contractor with basic security training. Under policy, contractors max at read without advanced security training and are never allowed admin. Even under the HR record (full-time Analyst), admin would not be permitted because Analyst does not own Source Code (owned by Engineer). Given the conflicting employment records and that admin is never permitted in either case, the most defensible maximum is read.
